title: Finneas to Keynote Guild of Music Supervisors’ 2026 State of Music in Media Conference
summary: Panelists set to appear include Nora Felder (Stranger Things), Kris Bowers (Spider-Noir) and Carlos Rafael Rivera (Hacks).
contentText:
Finneas is set to be the keynote speaker at the Guild of Music Supervisors’ 12th annual State of Music in Media Conference. The two-time Oscar winner and 11-time Grammy winner is scheduled to speak on Saturday, Aug. 15 at 11:00 a.m. on the campus of West Los Angeles College in Culver City, Calif. His keynote, titled “Inside the Importance of Music and Its Powerful Connection to Story: A Conversation with Finneas O’Connell,” will be moderated by Diallo Riddle, who received a Primetime Emmy nod in 2011 as a writer on Late Night With Jimmy Fallon .

“We are thrilled and honored to welcome Finneas as our keynote speaker,” Jonathan Leahy, president of the Guild of Music Supervisors, said in a statement. “His career perfectly demonstrates how each of us brings a unique voice to the creative process based on personal experiences and perspectives — and through collaboration those voices become the choir of truly impactful creative work.”

Programming highlights include spotlight panels with 2026 Emmy-nominated music supervisors, composers and songwriters, plus conversations about new landscapes to explore for music supervisors, how-to classes on fixing music clearance challenges, and opportunities to learn how to get music in front of music supervisors.

Panelists appearing at the conference include Andrew Bird ( The Pitt ), Nora Felder ( Stranger Things ), Manish Raval ( Nobody Wants This ), Michelle Johnson ( The Boys ), Yvette Metoyer ( The Boys ), Matt Biffa ( Hacks ), Toko Nagata ( Widow’s Bay ), Kris Bowers ( Spider-Noir ), Michael Dean Parsons ( Spider-Noir ), Dave Porter ( Pluribus ), Carlos Rafael Rivera ( Hacks ), David Stal ( Hacks ), and Miguel Gandelman ( Super Bowl LX Halftime Show with Bad Bunny ).

To buy tickets to the conference and learn more, visit the GMS Media Conference site.

The Guild of Music Supervisors is a nonprofit organization that was founded in 2010 with the goal of preserving and promoting the role of the music supervisor within all forms of media. The Guild holds numerous educational and networking events throughout the year.
